IsolationGateSurvivesThroughTheCLI is ~110 lines: 2 tests, 4 helpers, one docstring. Smaller than EngineDeliberateBreakage (~85 lines of body) and CoverageScriptDeliberateBreakage already in the same file. One coherent responsibility: the gate as driven through main().

override.repo_standard: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md:88-92 — 'A check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed. Before you offer a check as evidence, demonstrate it can reach a failing state.'
override.reason: The two fixtures are deliberately non-identical along the exact axis the new guard exists to measure: the old one calls E.start() in-process after os.chdir (base_dir is None), the new one shells out to main() --file so the engine computes base_dir = path.parent, and the new one needs a main-checkout-plus-linked-worktree topology the old one has no use for. Extracting a shared builder would couple them, and a later edit to that shared builder that threaded base_dir would move BOTH together — recreating precisely the blind spot this class was written to close (the result doc's section 4 shows the old test staying green while production is disarmed, which I reproduced: under the naive fix 1 failed, 6 passed, with the pre-existing test among the 6 green). Deliberate fixture independence is what makes the guard falsifiable, so the standard subordinates the DRY smell here.

smells.finding: Helpers operate on the class's own fixture state (self.main_checkout, self.worktree, self.spine_path). No method reaches predominantly into another object's data.

main_checkout / worktree / spine_path travel together conceptually but are held as instance attributes on a single test fixture and never passed around as a repeated argument group. No clump crosses a signature.

Paths are Path objects throughout; conversion to str/as_posix happens only at the subprocess and JSON boundaries, which genuinely require strings. The one raw string is the shell command text, which is inherently a string.
Widest new signature is _write_spine(self, here_expected: str) and _start_from(self, cwd: Path) — one argument each. _git uses *args, matching the existing helper in the same file.
The diff touches one test file plus a mechanically regenerated map/INDEX.md. Nothing in the change requires a coordinated edit anywhere else — verified: git diff for scripts/ and skills/ is empty.

tests/test_worktree_precondition_wiring.py continues to change for exactly one reason — the worktree-isolation precondition. The new class is another facet of that same reason (#329/#422 wiring, now #315 cwd), not a second unrelated axis of change.

json.loads(self.spine_path.read_text(...))['tasks']['init']['status'] is dict subscripting of a parsed JSON document, not a chain of objects asking objects for objects. Reading persisted state is the point of the assertion.

No unused hooks, parameters or abstraction layers. Both helpers have a caller inside the class; the pass-side test exists specifically to prove the refusal-side test is not a gate that never opens, which is required by CREW_CONTEXT:88-92 rather than speculative.
The class carries a 20-line docstring plus inline comments — a large comment-to-code ratio that would normally read as compensating for unclear code.

override.repo_standard: The g1 handoff's Constraints: 'Match the module's existing style: type hints, a real docstring explaining WHY (this module's docstrings carry rationale, not restatement)', consistent with the file's existing class docstrings and with CREW_CONTEXT's requirement that a guard's falsifiability be demonstrable.
override.reason: The docstring is not restating what the code does; it records why this test must stay SEPARATE from the one 30 lines above it and what a future agent should conclude if it goes red. That rationale is the guard's entire payload — a trap-marker whose message is unreadable is a trap that gets deleted. The repo standard explicitly asks for why-carrying docstrings, so the ratio is sanctioned. Noted separately as a review finding (not a smell): one sentence of that docstring — 'the test is right and the change is wrong' — is stated more absolutely than the guard can support, since the recommended option-1 fix could also turn it red for a stale-fixture reason.
